- Model consistently underestimates prices, especially in early periods of the 30-day window.
- Forecasts tend to be too low relative to recent history, suggesting underweighting of recent trends.
- Model shows significant lag in responding to recent price spikes; forecasts often overshoot or lag behind true price movements.
- After sharp price spikes, model tends to overcorrect downward, then undercorrect later — suggesting poor handling of momentum.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: overestimates mean price levels and fails to capture sustained upward/downward trends.
- Forecasts for later days (e.g., 25–30) are often too low, indicating poor extrapolation of recent momentum.
- Model underestimates price volatility in high-variance periods (e.g., 2024-02-06), leading to persistent underprediction.
- Forecasts are overly conservative in the face of recent upward momentum, failing to capture “breakout” or “rebound” phases.
